content:
Elliot Price: Quick Q for folks working on Standard Demo v1 docs: where do we want the demo tenant runbook to live as the source of truth? Confluence is easiest to edit, but the docs site stub (behind access) would be more "official" + versioned. Concern is keeping it updated as configs/scripts change.

Renee Sullivan: +1 on not letting it drift. Field folks are already bookmarking random docs. If we put it on the docs site, edits will be slower (PRs/review) but at least we can tie to releases.

Markus Klein: From SE side: Confluence is way more usable day-to-day. We need the runbook editable during a live incident ("demo tenant is slow") without waiting on a docs deploy.

Talia Benson: Also need a single link we can put in enablement email + LMS. But I’m worried Confluence perms get messy and people fork pages.

Soojin Lee: For the deck/talk track, we’re already pointing to Confluence pages. If we move runbook to docs site, we’ll need to update a bunch of internal links + make sure screenshots match.

Elliot Price: Totally. Docs site has better IA/search for new hires, but Confluence wins on speed. What if we do:
1) Confluence = canonical runbook (operational, clickpaths, troubleshooting)
2) Docs site = short landing page "Demo environment" that links to Confluence + key assets (reset checklist, known-good scenarios)

Renee Sullivan: That works as long as the docs site page is VERY explicit that it’s a directory/entry point, not a duplicate runbook.

Rafael Mendes: Speaking as runbook/on-call owner: I need to be able to update steps same day when we learn something (quota default, routing rule weirdness, dashboard import gotcha). Confluence is the only thing that supports that.

Sean Gallagher: Agree. Also, runbook has operational details we don’t want to accidentally expose broadly. Docs site is behind access, but it’s still easier to misconfigure and later open up. Confluence w/ tighter space perms is safer.

Chloe Martin: From Console dashboards angle: we’ve got import steps that keep changing (INT-782 was literally "missing panels"). I can update a Confluence section quickly when we fix queries.

Nikhil Sharma: One more: if docs site is the canonical, then any product behavior change that affects demo needs a PR. That’s good discipline but will slow urgent fixes. For demo tenant, we’ll have lots of small tweaks from dry runs.

Elliot Price: OK leaning Confluence canonical + docs site pointer. How do we prevent Confluence from becoming stale / multiple versions?

Talia Benson: Governance: single owner + scheduled review. E.g., "Runbook owners: Rafael (ops) + Renee (scenario scripts) + Elliot (docs)." Add a lightweight monthly review reminder + pre-demo checklist includes "verify runbook last updated".

Renee Sullivan: Could also add a required "runbook update" checkbox to ENG-4920/4922/4924 type tickets when demo-affecting changes ship.

Markus Klein: +1. And pin the page + lock editing to a small group. Everyone else can comment/suggest edits.

Soojin Lee: Also: talk track should reference a stable anchor link (not a draft page). If we go Confluence, can we use a shortlink?

Elliot Price: Yes. I can set up a Confluence short URL and make it the only one we circulate. We should also add a banner at the top: "Do not copy this page; link to it." (People *will* duplicate otherwise.)

Chloe Martin: For dashboards, I’ll add a section "Known-good dashboards" with a last-verified date + the import source (observability-pack export). Then weekly regression check can validate the panels match.

Rafael Mendes: Suggest adding an "Operational status" section with:
- dashboards to check pre-demo
- what green looks like
- fallback plan if console is lagging
- who to ping (business hours) + escalation

Sean Gallagher: And put a note that for incidents we follow the SRE "demo tenant" oncall path (lightweight) vs full production incident process.

Elliot Price: Action items:
- I’ll keep Confluence as canonical for runbook + add ownership + edit policy + banner.
- I’ll update the docs site stub to be a landing page that links out (no duplicated steps). This is basically what PR-1294 was starting; I’ll tweak language.
- Talia: add governance note to program plan (monthly review + ticket checkbox).

Talia Benson: Yep, I’ll add to the rollout checklist + make sure enablement email uses the docs site landing page (so we can change links behind it), and that landing page points to the Confluence canonical.

Renee Sullivan: :thumbsup: I’ll add a note to the demo scripts README to reference the landing page, not hardcoded Confluence paths.

Markus Klein: Works for field. Please keep the Confluence runbook readable fast (table of contents + "If demo breaks" section at top).

Elliot Price: Will do. I’ll post the final links here once the Confluence page banner + docs landing copy are updated.
